span: separate non-joint zone of consideration should be prepared for each Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe category
why: Petitioners' submission, in a reservation-in-promotion backlog dispute, that the reservation policy requires a separate zone; the court's response begins in the next paragraph.

span: if a reserved category candidate is in merit, he will occupy a general category seat
why: Open-merit selection in direct recruitment; not promotion.

span: benefit of reservation has been extended to scheduled castes and scheduled tribes, in promotions also
why: Appellants' counsel argues the State may extend reservation in promotion with consequential seniority; a party submission, not the court's view.

span: only those Scheduled Castes/Scheduled Tribes as notified in the Presidential Notification for the respective Union Territory can legitimately claim the benefit of reservation in that Union Territory
why: Which SC/ST members can claim reservation in a Union Territory; not promotion.

span: the order passed providing 100% reservation is arbitrary, illegal, impermissible, and unconstitutional
why: Holding about a 100% reservation for scheduled tribes in teacher posts in scheduled areas; not reservation in promotion.

span: reservation of posts in promotion is dependent on the inadequacy of representation of members of the Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes
why: Extract of Suraj Bhan Meena quoted within the present judgment; the court narrates that the High Court's view was accepted but this passage is the quotation.
